answers.answer: Speaker D (Marketing) raised the health complaint in Meeting B, reporting that repetitive strain injury (RSI) could result from frequent button pressing by channel-zapping users. The team responded by exploring touch controls and flat buttons, then ultimately adopting a rubber case with simple push-buttons that was explicitly marketed as anti-RSI. The final prototype earned the best possible RSI score of 1 on a 1-to-7 scale.

brief:
BRIEF FOR TEAM TS3012, before meeting d. Based on meetings a to c only.

WHAT HAS BEEN DECIDED (CURRENT)
- Project Manager Mark (Speaker A) set the goal to create an original, trendy, user-friendly TV remote targeting younger people as the main focus (meetings a, c). [TS3012a: "we need design a remote control for television set, so, which has to be original, trendy and user-friendly"; TS3012c: "We're definitely focussing on the younger people, 'cause that was our main goal"]
- Project Manager Mark (Speaker A) set production cost target at ~12.5€ and restated sales price at 25€ (meetings a, b). [TS3012a: "The production price, twelve and a half Euros, approximately."; TS3012b: "We are going for twenty five Euros sales price"]
- The team decided on a universal remote with volume and channel controls at the centre, using push-buttons (meeting b). [TS3012b: "I think it's universal. I think we should go for universal"; TS3012b: "we do agree that we keep this at the centre, because it's basically the most important function"]
- Industrial Designer Xavier (Speaker C) confirmed the remote will use push-buttons and round buttons, with the scroll wheel voted out (meeting c). [TS3012c: "Okay. So push-buttons we will use"; TS3012c: "No r no scroll-wheel. Okay. Um I don't see anything missing really"]
- Project Manager Mark (Speaker A) decided on a leaner shape with rounded top, curved design, rubber case, and batteries in the largest part (meeting c). [TS3012c: "I think so because it looks leaner and we should just go with that"; TS3012c: "The case, it will be the material will be rubber, suppose"]
- The team will implement beep and flash to locate the remote, the teletext button stays but not as a big button, and speech recognition is not implemented yet despite over 60% interest (meetings b, c). [TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote"; TS3012b: "Well, I don't think we should remove the button, because there are always people who are using it"]

WHAT CHANGED ALONG THE WAY
- Remote locator evolved from a generic finder and a TV-attached box to a beep and flash system (meetings b, c). [TS3012b: "we need to get something on the on the remote to find it somewhere"; TS3012c: "we are going to implement the beep and the flash thing to recover your remote"]
- Target customer refined from "under forty" to "younger people" as the main goal (meetings b, c). [TS3012b: "we want to appeal to younger people, which are um the younger people were defined under forty"; TS3012c: "We're definitely focussing on the younger people, 'cause that was our main goal"]
- Changeable covers dropped: the group moved from using interchangeable covers to excluding them from the basic design (meeting c). [TS3012c: "one of these interchangeable covers apparently which will make it a more fashionable product"; TS3012c: "that's not something we're working with in the basic design"]
- Case material settled on rubber after ruling out wood (meeting c). [TS3012c: "No, wood i wood's not an option"; TS3012c: "Okay, so we're definitely going for rubber"]
- Button layout specified from a basic structure to volume and channel controls at the centre (meeting b). [TS3012b: "we have decided more or less the basic structure"; TS3012b: "we do agree that we keep this at the centre, because it's basically the most important function"]

OPEN ACTIONS AND WHO OWNS THEM
- Project Manager Mark (Speaker A) will investigate whether to change buttons and cover together or only the cover (meeting b). [TS3012b: "Either either change both the buttons and and the cover or just the cover"]
- UI Designer Nick (Speaker B) will develop design concepts and collaborate with Industrial Designer Xavier (Speaker C) on the final internal and external design (meetings b, c). [TS3012b: "I'll put some on paper and present them next time"; TS3012c: "you should work together on the final design, both on internal and external design"]
- Industrial Designer Xavier (Speaker C) will research costs for rechargeable base station, LCD, and microphone options (meeting b). [TS3012b: "I'm going to try to find that out"; TS3012b: "Just to do research into both, w what it costs and what it takes for space"]

DISAGREEMENTS STILL OPEN
- UI Designer Nick (Speaker B) raised that many buttons are unclear and symbols fade over time, so labels must be durable; this remains unresolved (meeting b). [TS3012b: "There are many buttons on a remote control which are not clear"; TS3012b: "symbols tend to fade after a while"]
- Project Manager Mark (Speaker A) and Marketing Expert Dirk (Speaker D) disagree on mute button placement: Mark wants it at the bottom, Dirk wants it next to volume; power button placement also undecided (meeting b). [TS3012b: "I think it should be at the bottom somewhere"; TS3012b: "Or or with the volume selection"]
- The team is split on speech recognition: Mark proposed a microphone if feasible, Xavier suggested the remote could talk back, but Nick questioned the need (meetings b, c). [TS3012b: "we could put a microphone in here for example"; TS3012c: "do you actually need the remote talking back"]
- Marketing Expert Dirk (Speaker D) wants the LCD at the top for reading, but Mark argues buttons belong where fingers rest; the exact position and size are not final (meeting b). [TS3012b: "If you're reading from top to bottom, I think it's better to put it uh at the top"; TS3012b: "It's not that uh it's not the most important function, it's just an extra thing"]
- Industrial Designer Xavier (Speaker C) proposed a real product name, while colour choices range from a yellow remote with black buttons to a neutral base for interchangeable covers, against the corporate black and yellow (meetings b, c). [TS3012b: "let's give this uh a name, and not like some vague serial number"; TS3012c: "I would take a yellow remote control. To have it flashy"]
